summary: Over-count(9) + iterative dedup on champion adapter
hypothesis: Generating 9 questions (two native spares) and iteratively deduplicating should clear multi-redundant cases that exp046's single spare left behind, because the extra slot gives the dedup pass a second chance to evict a surviving near-duplicate pair.
technique: The champion adapter is prompted with schema count=9 (two over-count spares), then a deterministic iterative Swift dedup loop drops the later member of each redundant pair — using a high-recall union detector (binary same-info OR cosine ≥ 0.75 OR Jaccard ≥ 0.5) — until 7 remain, with any tail extras dropped by position.
result: Scored 0.423 on the full-30 greedy eval (4 wins / 2 ties / 23 losses vs Sonnet, 1 refusal), down from champion exp046's 0.430. Specificity fell from 4 to 3 — the extra count=9 perturbation pulled slots toward generic phrasing — while nonRed and coverage were unchanged; the hypothesis was falsified on two axes (iterative dedup still couldn't evict the deep-duplicate pairs the union detector under-fires on, and the extra off-distribution question cost spec-4). Discarded; exp046 remains champion.

stages.text: Iterative dedup: union detector, tail-drop to 7
